_comment: Transcribed verbatim from the approved course outline (Course Organization section). This is the contract the runbooks are checked against by scripts/check.mjs clip-outline-alignment. Do not edit to match a runbook -- edit the runbook. Presentation clips carry runbook: null -- they have no runbook, and clip-outline-alignment skips them; they are here so the map covers the whole outline and outline-map-matches-source can check all of it.

objectives.TO1: Apply Codex to plan and execute a codebase refactoring operation using reviewable passes
objectives.EO1a: Construct a refactoring prompt that instructs Codex to map noisy modules, identify dead code, and propose one cleanup theme at a time before editing
objectives.EO1b: Apply the ExecPlan pattern to maintain a running log of intended changes, behavior contracts, and validation checks across a multi-session refactor
objectives.EO1c: Evaluate a Codex-generated refactoring diff to confirm that public behavior is preserved and that architecture migrations are separated into discrete tasks
objectives.EO1d: Explain when to use Plan mode before committing Codex to implementation
objectives.TO2: Demonstrate how to orchestrate a legacy-to-modern stack migration with Codex using incremental checkpoints.
objectives.EO2a: Direct Codex to inventory a legacy system's routing, data models, auth, build tooling, tests, and external contracts before proposing a migration plan
objectives.EO2b: Evaluate a Codex-generated migration plan for compatibility layers, explicit behavioral exceptions, and rollback visibility
objectives.EO2c: Apply validation checks (lint, type-check, focused tests) after each migration milestone rather than batching cleanup
objectives.EO2d: Use the ASP.NET Core skill or equivalent framework skill to apply platform-specific migration guidance
objectives.TO3: Apply Codex automations to run recurring bug triage across multiple data sources at team scale.
objectives.EO3a: Configure a bug triage automation using the Sentry, Slack, Linear, and GitHub plugins to sweep a defined time window
objectives.EO3b: Evaluate a Codex-generated triage report for correct P0–P3 prioritization, deduplicated bug entries, and evidence-backed recommendations
objectives.EO3c: Convert a tested manual triage sweep into a scheduled automation using the same thread context
objectives.EO3d: Apply a routing workflow to draft Slack updates, Linear issues, or GitHub comments after triage approval
objectives.TO4: Demonstrate how to debug and trace Codex automations
objectives.EO4a: Use the Codex review pane to inspect uncommitted diffs from an automation run, including per-hunk staging and revert controls

m1-c1.title: Plan reviewable refactors with Codex
bullets: Use Plan mode when discovery and architectural understanding should happen before implementation
Map the review flow from codebase evidence to bounded cleanup theme, implementation, validation, and diff review
Keep behavior preservation and architecture migrations as separate review decisions

m1-c2.title: Demo: Map noisy TypeScript modules with Codex before editing
bullets: Open the TypeScript service in Codex and ask it to map modules, dependencies, public behavior, and dead-code candidates
Constrain Codex to propose one cleanup theme before editing any files
Inspect repository evidence and reject unrelated architectural changes before implementation
Confirm Plan mode produces a bounded, reviewable first pass

m1-c3.title: Demo: Execute a Codex refactor with ExecPlan checkpoints
bullets: Create an ExecPlan that records intended changes, behavior contracts, validation checks, and progress across the refactor
Let Codex implement one bounded cleanup pass and run Vitest plus TypeScript validation
Inspect the generated diff and confirm public behavior is preserved
Remove the architecture migration Codex bundled into the cleanup diff and log it as a separate ExecPlan task

m1-c4.title: Plan a legacy Express migration with Codex checkpoints
bullets: Shift from the refactoring project to the legacy CommonJS JavaScript Express 4 service and define ESM TypeScript on Express 5 as the target
Separate inventory, CommonJS-to-ESM compatibility planning, validation, and rollback into explicit checkpoints before implementation
Treat behavioral exceptions and the CommonJS-to-ESM compatibility layer as deliberate migration decisions

m1-c5.title: Demo: Inventory a legacy Express 4 service with Codex
bullets: Direct Codex to inventory the legacy CommonJS JavaScript Express 4 service across Express routes, data models, auth, build tooling, tests, and external contracts
Review the generated migration plan for the CommonJS-to-ESM compatibility layer, explicit behavioral exceptions, and rollback visibility
Split the ESM TypeScript Express 5 migration into incremental milestones that can be validated independently
Reject the milestone that batches route migration with dependency upgrades and have Codex split it into two checkpoints

m1-c6.title: Demo: Migrate one Express route to TypeScript with framework guidance
bullets: Apply an equivalent Node.js and TypeScript framework skill to migrate one Express route slice from JavaScript to TypeScript
Run ESLint, TypeScript type-checking, build validation, and focused Vitest tests immediately after the route migration
Inspect the diff and verify the CommonJS-to-ESM compatibility contract before accepting the route change
Record the checkpoint so the Express 5 migration can continue or roll back from a known state

m2-c1.title: Design reviewable Codex automations at team scale
bullets: Map the triage architecture from Sentry and GitHub evidence through correlation, P0–P3 prioritization, review, approval, and routed drafts to Slack and Linear
Keep source evidence attached to each P0–P3 recommendation so team decisions remain reviewable
Separate approved downstream actions from the triage decision itself

m2-c2.title: Demo: Run a manual Codex triage sweep across Sentry and GitHub
bullets: Configure Sentry and GitHub evidence sources, connect Slack and Linear routing destinations, and define the triage time window
Run the sweep manually so the same thread context captures source evidence before scheduling
Inspect the report for P0–P3 priority, deduplicated bugs, and evidence-backed recommendations
Correct weak prioritization or duplicate entries before automation is promoted

m2-c3.title: Demo: Schedule Codex triage and route work to Slack and Linear
bullets: Convert the tested manual sweep into a scheduled Codex automation using the same thread context
Run the scheduled workflow and compare its report with the validated manual pattern
Approve selected findings before drafting Slack updates or Linear issues
Verify Slack and Linear drafts preserve the evidence and priority from the triage decision

m2-c4.title: Debug Codex automations through review evidence
bullets: Use automation inputs, generated changes, validation results, and review state as the debugging evidence chain
Distinguish a bad source assumption from a bad generated change before deciding what to rerun
Use per-hunk review to keep valid changes while rejecting unsafe or unrelated edits

m2-c5.title: Demo: Inspect automation diffs in the Codex review pane
bullets: Open an automation run that produced uncommitted changes and inspect the diff in the Codex review pane
Review changed files and hunks against the triage evidence that caused the automation to act
Use source control to stage valid hunks individually and revert an unrelated or incorrect hunk
Confirm only approved changes remain before the repository is committed

m2-c6.title: Demo: Trace a failed Codex automation and recover safely
bullets: Start from a failed automation result and trace the source evidence, generated change, and validation outcome
Use the review pane to isolate the incorrect hunk instead of discarding the entire run
Revert the bad change, preserve valid work, and rerun with corrected context
Verify the recovered run produces a clean reviewable diff before acceptance
